claims.statement: The step certificate group is registered via init() in command/certificate/certificate.go with Name "certificate" and usage "create, revoke, validate, bundle, and otherwise manage certificates", exposing 13 subcommands: bundle, create, format, inspect, fingerprint, lint, needs-renewal, sign, verify, key, install, uninstall, and p12.
step certificate create operates offline with profiles defined as constants: leaf (the default), self-signed, intermediate-ca, root-ca, and csr (used only by the sign subcommand).
Default validity periods for certificate create are 24 hours for leaf, 24 hours for self-signed, 10 years for intermediate-ca, 10 years for root-ca, and 24 hours when a custom template is used.
In create, --profile and --template are incompatible flags, the self-signed profile requires --subtle, and --bundle is only valid with the leaf profile.

create --csr requires a private key and rejects --ca, --ca-key, --ca-password-file, --not-before, --not-after, --bundle, and any profile other than leaf; the subject becomes the default SAN and x509util.DefaultCertificateRequestTemplate is used when no template is given.
create requires --skip-csr-signature when a public key is supplied via --key without a private part, and --no-password requires --insecure.

When no --template is given, create maps each profile to a built-in x509util template (leaf to DefaultLeafTemplate, intermediate-ca to DefaultIntermediateTemplate, root-ca to DefaultRootTemplate, self-signed to DefaultLeafTemplate), and template user data comes from --set/--set-file via flags.GetTemplateData.

parseOrCreateKey generates a key pair from --kty/--curve/--size via keyutil.GenerateKeyPair (with keyutil.Insecure() permitting short RSA keys under --insecure) or loads --key through the KMS-aware cryptoutil.CreateSigner, falling back to public-key loading when the key cannot sign.

parseSigner enforces that leaf and intermediate-ca profiles require --ca and --ca-key while root-ca and self-signed reject them, and builds the issuer signer from --ca-key via cryptoutil.CreateSigner with optional --ca-kms and --ca-password-file.

create signs the certificate with x509util.CreateCertificate using the parent (self-signing for root/self-signed), skips writing the key when it is a KMS signer, appends the parent certificate to the output file under --bundle, and encrypts saved keys with a prompted password unless --no-password or --password-file is set.

step certificate sign <csr-file> <crt-file> <key-file> allows profiles leaf (default), intermediate-ca, and csr; --profile and --template are incompatible; built-in JSON templates set key usages for leaves and basicConstraints with maxPathLen for intermediates.

sign validates the CSR signature, checks that the issuer private key matches the issuer certificate (validateIssuerKey), and requires the issuer to be a CA with keyCertSign; for intermediate-ca the issuer pathLenConstraint must permit the requested --path-len (default 0, -1 for unlimited).
In sign, --not-after defaults to 24 hours for leaf and 10 years for intermediate-ca profiles, and the signed certificate is written to stdout with --bundle appending the issuer certificate.

verify validates a local certificate file (first PEM block as leaf, remaining blocks as intermediates) or a remote address via the shared getPeerCertificates helper, builds the root pool from --roots, and runs path validation with KeyUsages Any.
verify supports opt-in --verify-ocsp and --verify-crevocation flags, and obtains the issuing CA from --issuing-ca or the IssuingCertificateURL AIA extension of the certificate.
VerifyOCSPEndpoint POSTs an OCSP request to --ocsp-endpoint or the OCSPServer AIA endpoints and fails verification when the response status is Revoked or Unknown.

VerifyCRLEndpoint downloads CRLs from --crl-endpoint or the certificate's CRLDistributionPoints, validates the CRL signature against the issuer unless --insecure is set, and fails when the certificate serial appears in the revoked list.

inspect prints certificate or CSR details from a file, stdin, or a remote address (with --insecure); --format supports text, json, and pem with --short restricted to text; text output uses certinfo and JSON output uses zcrypto.

lint uses zlint to check a single certificate — the first PEM block of a file or the first peer certificate of a remote address — for common errors and prints a JSON ResultSet; it is intended for Web PKI certificates and may not be appropriate for internal PKIs.

bundle concatenates the first PEM blocks of a leaf certificate and an intermediate CA into a chain file; format converts between PEM and DER for certificates and CSRs; key extracts the public key from the first block of a certificate or key file.

fingerprint prints SHA-256 fingerprints of a local certificate or remote peer; --sha1 switches to SHA-1 and requires --insecure, --bundle prints all certificates in bundle order, and the output encoding comes from --format.

install and uninstall add or remove a root certificate in the system default trust store with optional --java and --firefox trust stores; getTruststoreOptions rejects certificates that are not self-signed CAs, and failures of the underlying trust store command are surfaced as truststore.CmdError with the executed arguments.

p12 packages either a certificate plus private key (identity store, first certificate as server cert, rest as intermediates) or only --ca bundles (trust store with subject-fingerprint friendly names) into PKCS#12, using the modern encoder by default and PBE+SHA1+RC2/3DES algorithms under --legacy.

needs-renewal is a scriptable renewal probe that exits 0 when renewal is needed, 1 when within lifetime, 2 when the certificate file does not exist, and 255 for other errors; the default threshold is 66% of the allotted lifetime used, --expires-in accepts a percent or duration, and --bundle checks every certificate in the chain.

Remote address support is shared by certificate subcommands: urlPrefixes maps tcp/tls/https to port 443, smtps to 465, and ldaps to 636; getPeerCertificates dials TLS (minimum TLS 1.2) honoring --roots, --servername, and --insecure and returns the peer certificate chain; trimURL resolves the default port and returns ("", false) for plain file paths.

Adding a new certificate subcommand means defining an xCommand() in command/certificate/ following the existing pattern and appending it to the Subcommands slice in certificate.go, since the init()-driven group registration picks up the subcommands automatically.

Changing a create profile requires updating the profile/validity constants, the --profile usage text, the profile-to-template mapping in createAction, and the per-profile issuer flag rules in parseSigner; sign profiles are validated separately with their own template selection and issuer path-length rules.
